name: Isolated Filum Lipoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Radiological and Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Isolated Filum Lipoma

criteria.description: Identification of a fatty mass within the filum terminale on MRI
Presence of tethered cord syndrome symptoms without other spinal dysraphism
No associated spinal dysraphism or other neural tube defects on imaging
Neurological examination showing lower limb weakness or sensory changes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: MRI evidence of filum terminale lipoma with clinical signs of tethered cord syndrome and absence of other spinal malformations
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on MRI findings combined with clinical presentation; biopsy is rarely performed.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Radiological evidence of fatty infiltration of the filum terminale
searchTerms: fat buildup in spinal cord tissue seen on scan
fatty changes in lower spinal cord
fatty infiltration in spinal cord on imaging

pathognomonic.symptomName: Tethered cord syndrome with progressive neurological deficits
searchTerms: spinal cord tethering with worsening nerve problems
tight spinal cord causing progressive weakness
spinal cord stuck causing neurological decline

common.symptomName: Lower limb sensory disturbances including paresthesia
searchTerms: leg sensory changes including pins and needles

common.symptomName: Bladder dysfunction including urinary urgency or retention
searchTerms: urinary urgency or difficulty emptying bladder

occasional.symptomName: Back pain localized to the lumbosacral region
Constipation related to neurogenic bowel dysfunction
searchTerms: bowel movement difficulty from nerve issues

imaging: MRI showing fatty infiltration of the filum terminale
MRI demonstrating low-lying conus medullaris with tethered cord
Absence of other spinal dysraphism or neural tube defects on imaging
other: Neurological examination revealing lower limb weakness and sensory deficits
Urodynamic studies may show neurogenic bladder dysfunction

distinguishingFeatures: Tethered cord syndrome caused by other spinal dysraphisms such as lipomyelomeningocele
Presence of associated spinal anomalies on imaging
Open or closed spinal dysraphism with visible spinal cord malformations
Often associated with cutaneous stigmata or bony defects

redFlags: Progressive lower limb weakness or paralysis
Rapidly worsening bladder or bowel dysfunction
Signs of spinal cord ischemia or acute neurological deterioration
references: Yamada S, et al. Tethered cord syndrome and filum terminale lipoma: diagnosis and management. Neurosurg Clin N Am. 2010.
Tubbs RS, et al. Filum terminale lipomas: clinical and radiological features. Childs Nerv Syst. 2015.
